score_scale: 1 (poor) to 5 (excellent); 'ease' = gentle learning curve, 'ops' = low operational burden

items.name: Next.js (React)
items.summary: React meta-framework with server rendering, static generation, React Server Components and file-based routing.
strengths: SSR/SSG/ISR give crawlers full HTML (strong SEO, fast LCP)
Largest React ecosystem and hiring pool
Same codebase can host API routes / server actions for small apps
weaknesses: App Router + Server Components add conceptual load
Some features (ISR, image optimisation, middleware) are smoothest on Vercel

weaknesses.text: No search visibility needed: server rendering brings a Node.js server and the server/client component split for pages a client-rendered React app would ship as static files

server_rendering.why: Server rendering sends finished HTML so crawlers and first-time visitors from search see content without running JavaScript; its cost is a server runtime for every page request (or a static export that drops server features) and the server/client component boundary. With no search visibility asked for, the same React components render in the browser from static files.

items.name: React SPA (Vite)
items.summary: Client-rendered single-page React app built with Vite; deploys as static files to any CDN.
strengths: Static build: cheapest and simplest hosting
Huge component ecosystem (dashboards, charts, admin UIs)
No server to operate for the UI
weaknesses: Client-side rendering hurts SEO and first paint on slow phones
Routing, data fetching and state are your own architecture decisions

items.name: Nuxt (Vue)
items.summary: Vue meta-framework with SSR/SSG, auto-imports and the Nitro server engine (deploys to many targets).
strengths: Gentle learning curve (Vue templates)
SSR/SSG for SEO
Nitro deploys to Node, serverless and edge with presets
weaknesses: Smaller hiring pool than React
Fewer enterprise component libraries than React/Angular

server_rendering.why: Server rendering sends finished HTML so crawlers and first-time visitors from search see content without running JavaScript; its cost is a server runtime for page requests (or a static build that drops server features). With no search visibility asked for, a client-rendered app served as static files does the same job.

items.name: SvelteKit
items.summary: Svelte's application framework: compiled components, SSR/SSG, adapters for Node, static and serverless targets.
strengths: Smallest JS bundles in this list, best runtime performance
SSR + progressive enhancement by default
Adapters avoid platform lock-in
weaknesses: Smaller hiring pool and ecosystem than React, Vue or Angular
Fewer battle-tested enterprise UI kits

server_rendering.why: Server rendering sends finished HTML so crawlers and first-time visitors from search see content without running JavaScript; its cost is a server runtime for page requests (or a static build that drops server features). With no search visibility asked for, a client-rendered app served as static files does the same job.

items.name: Angular
items.summary: Google's batteries-included TypeScript framework (DI, router, forms, HTTP, SSR) aimed at large codebases.
strengths: Opinionated structure keeps large teams consistent
Everything first-party (router, forms, HTTP, i18n)
Long-term support releases suit enterprises
weaknesses: Steepest learning curve (RxJS, DI, modules/signals)
Heavier for small marketing/content sites

items.name: Astro
items.summary: Content-first framework that ships zero JS by default and hydrates interactive 'islands' only where needed.
strengths: Best Core Web Vitals for content/blog/docs/marketing sites
Use React/Vue/Svelte components inside islands
Static output hosts anywhere for ~free
weaknesses: Not designed for highly interactive app-like UIs
Smaller hiring pool

items.name: Server-rendered HTML + HTMX
items.summary: HTML rendered by the backend (Django/Rails/Phoenix/Go templates) with HTMX attributes for partial page updates; no SPA build step.
strengths: One codebase, one language; no JS build pipeline
Excellent for CRUD internal tools and admin panels
Pages are real HTML, so SEO is free
weaknesses: Rich client interactions (drag-drop editors, offline) get awkward
Requires a server-rendering backend; does not pair with BaaS

items.name: React Native (Expo)
items.summary: Cross-platform native mobile apps in React/TypeScript; Expo provides builds, OTA updates and native modules.
strengths: One codebase for iOS + Android (+ web via react-native-web)
Reuses React skills and TypeScript types from the web app
Expo EAS handles builds and over-the-air updates
weaknesses: Heavy animations / complex native integrations need native modules
App-store review cycle still applies to native changes

items.name: Flutter
items.summary: Google's cross-platform UI toolkit in Dart with its own rendering engine for consistent, fast UIs.
strengths: Pixel-consistent UI on iOS and Android
Smooth 60/120fps rendering
weaknesses: Dart is a new language for most web teams
Flutter Web output is poor for SEO

items.name: Native iOS + Android (Swift / Kotlin)
items.summary: Two native codebases using SwiftUI and Jetpack Compose.
strengths: Best performance, platform APIs and offline/background capabilities
Day-one access to new OS features
weaknesses: Two codebases, roughly double the effort
Needs at least one specialist per platform

platform_languages.why: One app per platform, each in its own language (Swift for iOS, Kotlin for Android)
